name: Myanmar
official: Republic of the Union of Myanmar

story: On 1 February 2021, the day Myanmar's newly elected parliament was to sit, the army arrested Aung San Suu Kyi, whose party had won 396 of 476 seats, and seized power, claiming fraud. The coup set off a civil war that has killed tens of thousands and displaced millions. Five years later, the general who led it found a way to make his rule look civilian.

After a three-phase election in December and January organised by the junta and dismissed by observers as neither free nor fair, the army-backed Union Solidarity and Development Party dominated a parliament where a quarter of seats are reserved for soldiers. On 3 April, it elected Senior General Min Aung Hlaing president with 429 of 584 votes (AFP via NST). The vote took place in a parliament building in Naypyidaw repaired after the 2025 earthquake. Because the constitution forbids a president from also leading the army, he handed command on 30 March to Ye Win Oo, a former intelligence chief seen as fiercely loyal (Reuters via Chronicle.lu). China, his key ally, promptly congratulated him. Suu Kyi, now 81, remains in prison. Analysts expect the new government to court neighbours for recognition while pressing the war against ethnic armies and resistance forces that still hold large parts of the country.
briefing.power: A presidential system under the military-written 2008 constitution. Parliament elects the president; the military holds 25 percent of seats, a veto over constitutional change, and control of the defence, interior and border ministries.
briefing.holders: President Min Aung Hlaing, with the army under Commander-in-Chief Ye Win Oo.
